_: Which piper voices actually work in a browser. Vendored, not maintained twice:
vorlaut and mitreden both need this answer and it is the same answer, so the file
is copied between them rather than each keeping its own. tts.py makes the same
argument about VOICE_CATALOGUE - one list, one place - and this is that argument
applied to the browser, where the list is different because the constraints are.
Three things make a voice usable in a tab, and piper's own catalogue answers none
of them:
quality  Only medium and high survive @diffusionstudio/vits-web today. Every
low and x_low voice dies with 'idx=140 must be within the inclusive
range [-130,129]'. Measured in mitreden's spike, docs/spike/README.md
on branch spike/piper-wasm.
The cause is narrower than this file used to say, and the difference
matters: nothing is missing from the older models. The German ich-Laut
can be written two ways in Unicode, precomposed as U+00E7 or as a c
plus the combining cedilla U+0327, and the phonemizer emits the second.
Thorsten's map holds both, the combining mark at 140. Kerstin's older
map has 130 entries, ids 0 to 129 - which is exactly the range in the
error - and holds only the precomposed form, at 40. Checked here: her
map is a strict subset of his, and both give that sound id 40.
So it is one sound spelled two ways, not a phoneme her model lacks, and
composing it where a model does not know the emitted form is a few
lines. Lautstark/stimmquelle has it as remapPhonemeIds, with Thorsten's
ids byte-identical on eight sentences and all of Kerstin's in range.
No audio has been rendered through it yet - doing that means owning the
onnxruntime call rather than vits-web's predict(), which phonemizes and
infers in one - so every low voice below stays rejected until it has.
reach    vits-web can only fetch what is in its hardcoded PATH_MAP. Its voices()
call returns the mirror's voices.json instead - 124 entries against 119
in the map - so five voices are advertised by the library and cannot be
downloaded by it. en_US-john-medium is one of them, and it is in
vorlaut's VOICE_CATALOGUE.
licence  Unchanged by any of this and easy to forget once a voice is a string in
a JSON file. Read the MODEL_CARD next to the model, not the file name.
'proof' says how each entry was established, because a list that says 'tested' and
means 'assumed' is worth less than no list:
spike    run in a browser in mitreden's spike
here     run in a browser from vorlaut's tools/ttscheck.html
rule     medium or high, present in PATH_MAP, never actually spoken in a tab
catalogue-only  fetched by tts.py, cannot be reached from a browser

voices.name: Thorsten (emotional)
voices.note: One model, several moods, chosen by speaker id. vits-web speaks the first one and offers no way to pick another.

voices.name: MLS
voices.note: A corpus, not a person - many speakers in one model, and no name a picker can show. The only German voice here that is not Thorsten, and the closest thing to a German female voice that runs at all.

voices.name: LJ Speech
voices.note: The name of a dataset, which reads like a mistake in a list of first names - tts.py says so about the same voice. Here as the free English fallback if Kristin ever goes, not as something to offer.

rejected.name: Kerstin
rejected.note: In vorlaut's VOICE_CATALOGUE and the only German female voice there. Published as low only, so no other file of hers would help. But her model is not the problem: her phoneme map is a strict subset of Thorsten's and spells the ich-Laut the precomposed way, at the same id 40 he uses. Recoverable, and the most valuable voice on this list to recover - see the note at the top.

rejected.name: Eva K
rejected.note: The other German female voice in the catalogue. x_low, so the same wall.

rejected.name: Ramona
rejected.note: The third and last German female voice piper publishes. Also low.

rejected.name: John
rejected.note: In vorlaut's VOICE_CATALOGUE and fetched fine by tts.py - it is on both mirrors, 63531379 bytes. It is vits-web that cannot have it: predict() looks the id up in PATH_MAP, finds nothing, and asks the mirror for 'undefined.json'. voices() lists it anyway.

rejected.name: HFC female
rejected.note: Runs in a browser - the spike used it. Non-commercial and share-alike, which is not what a voice handed on inside an application can be. tts.py already warns about exactly this: read the MODEL_CARD, not the file name.

rejected.name: Ryan
rejected.note: Every quality Ryan is published in - low, medium and high - is non-commercial and share-alike. A medium and a high English male voice is exactly what somebody reaches for when the list looks short, which is why it is written down here rather than left out. Between Ryan and the two HFC voices, roughly a third of piper's English medium and high catalogue cannot be handed on.
